note.text:
Air is a mixture of gases. By volume, dry air is about:
• nitrogen 78%
• oxygen 21%
• argon and other noble gases about 0.9%
• carbon dioxide about 0.04%
It also contains water vapour and dust, which vary.
Finding the percentage of oxygen: pass a known volume of air (for example 100 cm³) many times over heated copper in a tube between two gas syringes. The copper turns black (copper oxide) as it takes the oxygen. When cool, the volume left is about 79 cm³.
Oxygen used = volume at start − volume at end.
Percentage of oxygen = oxygen used ÷ volume at start × 100.

worked_example.problem: {v} cm³ of air is passed over heated copper until no more change. {w} cm³ of gas is left. Find the percentage of oxygen.

cards.idea: Air is a mixture: about {78}% nitrogen, {21}% oxygen and small amounts of argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
Heated copper takes the oxygen from the air and turns black; the volume of gas goes down.
example: The gas left is mainly nitrogen.

cards.idea: Oxygen used = volume at start − volume at end; percentage = oxygen used ÷ start volume × {100}.
example: Start {100} cm³, end {79} cm³: oxygen {21} cm³.

check.prompt: {v} cm³ of air is passed over heated copper. {w} cm³ of gas is left. What volume of oxygen was used?

misconceptions.explain: That is the gas left: subtract it from the start volume.

solution: Oxygen used = volume at start − volume at end.

pick.q: Which gas makes up the largest part of air?
e: Carbon dioxide is a tiny part.

pick.q: About what percentage of air is oxygen?
e: Oxygen is about one fifth, not half.

pick.q: Which noble gas is found in air (about 0.9%)?
e: Chlorine is not a noble gas.
Hydrogen is not a noble gas.
pick.y: Argon is the main noble gas in air.

pick.q: In the experiment, what happens to the heated copper?
e: The tube is not hot enough to melt copper.

pick.q: Which gas is mainly left in the syringe at the end?
e: The oxygen was used by the copper.
Carbon dioxide is a tiny part.
pick.y: Nitrogen does not react with copper.

questions.prompt: {v} cm³ of air is passed over heated copper. {w} cm³ of gas is left. What volume of oxygen was used?

misconceptions.explain: That is the gas left: subtract it from the start volume.

solution: Oxygen used = volume at start − volume at end.

questions.prompt: {v} cm³ of air is passed over heated copper until no more change. {w} cm³ of gas is left. What percentage of the air was oxygen?

misconceptions.explain: That is the volume: divide by the start volume and × {100}.
That is the gas left (mainly nitrogen): use the oxygen used.
